- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior 3-day high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.36) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought overreaction.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after 3+ consecutive days above 70), model often fails to recognize it; add 1–2% downward adjustment if 3+ days above 70.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model’s first 5 days are consistently above true outcome, apply a 1–3% downward correction to the first 3–5 days to avoid early overestimation.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.18–0.36), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 5-day moving average or use sentiment-weighted average (0.6×sentiment + 0.4×price) for adjustment.
